blocks.text: Small apartment: how to make every meter count

parts.html: In a small apartment, every square meter counts, and design calls for a creative approach. Here are some ideas to help make it comfortable and stylish.

Start with the layout: divide the apartment into functional zones — kitchen, living room, bedroom, and workspace. Movable partitions, sliding doors, or dual-purpose furniture work well for this. In a studio apartment, for example, you can combine the kitchen and living room into a single multifunctional space.

blocks.text: Transforming furniture: a lifesaver for small spaces

parts.html: Wall beds, sofa beds, and convertible tables save space and adapt to different needs. A bed that folds into a cabinet during the day turns the bedroom into a spacious living room or home office.

Storage is the main challenge in small apartments. Make use of the height: floor-to-ceiling shelves, cabinets, and overhead storage hold more without taking up floor space. Hidden storage can go under the bed and sofa, while organizers and containers keep things tidy inside. Built-in wardrobes and custom furniture designed around your needs put every corner to use.

Light and color make a space look larger. Light-colored walls, floors, and furniture combined with daylight create a sense of spaciousness, and a mirror opposite the window enhances the effect. Make the main lighting bright and even, while table lamps and wall sconces add coziness and highlight individual zones.

Choose compact appliances and multifunctional kitchen tools. Arrange cabinets and shelves so that everything you need is close at hand, and put the folding table and chairs away when you don’t need them.

You can find room for storage here too: shelves above the door, a cabinet under the sink, corner shelves. Mirrored cabinets and light-colored finishes will make the bathroom look roomier and brighter.
Light, sheer curtains, small rugs, and minimal decor create a sense of lightness and air. Avoid large, bulky decor — it overwhelms the space.

Folding chairs, tables on casters, and rolling cabinets make it easy to change the layout to suit what you need at the moment. This is especially helpful in studio apartments, where the space needs to stay flexible.

blocks.text: Making the most of corners and niches

parts.html: Corners and niches often go unused, even though they make excellent storage spots: corner shelves, cabinets, and built-in niches help put every corner to use.
The fewer items in a room, the more spacious it feels. Let go of excess furniture and decor, and make sure whatever you keep is both functional and stylish.
Let one zone do several jobs: a table in the living room serves for both dining and work, and a sofa bed is a place to relax by day and to sleep at night.

Light and neutral colors visually enlarge a space, but don’t be afraid to use bright accents in the interior. A few vivid pieces, such as cushions, rugs, or paintings, will give the apartment personality and bring the interior to life.
Live plants add coziness. Choose compact, low-maintenance ones and place them in wall planters and hanging pots — that way they don’t take up usable space.
